cards.text: One day Jesus is praying in private, and His disciples are with Him. Then He asks them a question. Friend, it's the kind where you can FEEL a second question coming right behind it.

cards.question: Jesus is praying in private, and His disciples are with Him. What does He ask them first?

answers.text: Who the crowds say He is
Which of them is the greatest

cards.text: The disciples have heard what people are saying about Jesus, and the answers are ALL over the place. It's like asking the group chat to pick one movie: nine opinions, zero movies.

cards.question: Some people in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist, the man who went around the Jordan preaching baptism (Luke 3:3).

cards.text: Others say He's Elijah, the prophet from long ago (1 Kings 18:36), and still others say a prophet of old has arisen. Everybody's got a theory, friend.
Then Jesus turns it around: “Who do you say I am?” Oh, NOW it's personal, like your boss saying “Got a minute?” and the whole office suddenly gets real interested in their shoes.

cards.question: Jesus asks His disciples, “Who do you say I am?” Which disciple answers Him?
The crowds have their theories. But Peter answers that Jesus is “The ___ of God.”

cards.text: Peter just said something HUGE. Then Jesus speaks to the disciples, and He is strict about it.

cards.question: After Peter says Jesus is the Christ of God, Jesus tells the disciples to go tell everyone.

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about the Son of Man, a name He uses for Himself (Luke 5:24). He says the Son of Man must suffer many things.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man must suffer many things. Who does He say will reject Him?

answers.text: The elders and chief priests and scribes
The Roman governor and his soldiers
The tax collectors and the sinners

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man must be killed and on the ___ day be raised to life.

cards.text: Jesus has just told the disciples the Son of Man must suffer, be killed and be raised to life. Now He speaks to all of them about what it takes to come after Him. Friend, this is not the fine print. This is the BIG print.

cards.question: Jesus says if anyone wants to come after Him, he must ___ himself.
Jesus says whoever wants to come after Him must deny himself, follow Him and take something up daily. What is it?

cards.text: Daily, friend, like an alarm clock with NO snooze button. Then Jesus says something about saving your life that flips everything upside down.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever wants to save his life will ___ it.
Jesus says whoever loses his life for His sake will save it.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks about the biggest deal anyone could ever make: gaining the whole world. Back in the junk drawer, MY biggest deal was trading one dusty takeout menu for a slightly less dusty one.

cards.question: Jesus says gaining the whole world is worth it, even if a man loses his very self.

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about anyone who is ashamed of Him and His words. And He points ahead to when the Son of Man comes in His glory.

cards.question: Jesus says if anyone is ashamed of Him and His words, what will the Son of Man do when He comes in His glory?
The Son of Man comes in His own glory. Whose glory does Jesus say He comes in too?

answers.text: The Father and the holy angels

cards.text: Then Jesus opens with “But I tell you truly,” and friend, when He starts like THAT, me and my gold base lean in TOGETHER. He says some standing there will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.

cards.question: Jesus says everyone standing there will see the kingdom of God before they taste death.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "The ___ of God.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences. It is not the passage's opening card, so the limit is 2. Its first sentence also recaps Luke 9:22, which Stop 1 cards 11 to 13 already covered, and the card cites Luke 9:22-23 because of that recap.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens by restating Luke 9:22 ("Jesus has just told the disciples the Son of Man must suffer, be killed and be raised to life"). That is a recap of the last stop, not a move forward.

The story card says "He says some standing there will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God." The very next card, card 13, asks whether Jesus says everyone standing there will see it. The story card has already given the answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The setup says Jesus says something about saving your life "that flips everything upside down." On card 5, both wrong answers ("keep" and "guard") are the not-flipped outcome, so the setup rules them out and leaves only "lose."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank in "he must ___ himself" asks the baker to guess the wording of Jesus' line. The story card before it ("this is the BIG print") gives nothing the baker could use to reason toward "deny" over "prove" or "trust."

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards can only be answered by luck or prior knowledge. In each case the story card before it gives no context for the answer: card 2 (what Jesus asks), card 4 (John the Baptist, after a card that only says the answers are all over the place), card 7 (Peter), card 12 (elders, chief priests and scribes) and card 13 (third day). That is 5 of the stop's 7 choice cards, so these are not "a few."

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Peter first appears only as an answer on card 7. After that, the cards refer to him by name without ever saying who he is, for example one of Jesus' disciples.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
